description: Tukar — confidential cross-border corridor. ZK verifiers (BN254 Groth16) + stateful pool with token custody on Stellar testnet.

token.note: real testnet USDC asset (issuer GC7SWGHR...), SAC; deposits move the real amount, bound to the commitment via a disclosure proof

merkleUpdate.note: proves oldRoot + newLeaf -> newRoot (trustless root registration)

pool.description: Hardened corridor pool with token custody + FULLY TRUSTLESS tree updates (no admin root backdoor — the only way to advance the root is a merkleUpdate proof). Builds the verifier public inputs from typed signals so nullifiers/commitments/root/amount are BOUND to the proof; root registry + nullifier set + commitment set (idempotent, no double-count) + pinned ASP allow/deny; pulls/releases real tokens on deposit/withdraw.

tested.deposit: success — compliance proof bound to commitment; pulled 100 tokens into the pool (balance 0 -> 100)
tested.withdraw: success — released tokens; publicAmount is NEGATIVE (r - amount: value leaving the shielded set, the correct JoinSplit sign), and the pool binds the released amount to that field-negative so it cannot release more than the proof authorizes
tested.registerRootVerified: success — trustless root advance via merkleUpdate proof (oldRoot -> newRoot)
tested.trustlessTreeAttack: registering a FAKE new_root with the real proof -> rejected (InvalidProof, Error #0)
tested.amountBindingFix: withdraw with amount=999 but public_amount=50 -> rejected (AmountNotBound, Error #6)
tested.bindingFix: transfer/withdraw with a valid proof but TAMPERED nullifiers -> rejected (InvalidProof, Error #0): nullifiers are part of the verified public inputs, so a double-spend bypass is impossible
tested.noAdminBackdoor: register_root (admin override) removed — root advances ONLY via register_root_verified with a merkleUpdate proof
tested.idempotentCommitment: deposit then register_root_verified of the same leaf records it once (commitment_count is not double-counted)
tested.globalAccumulator: register_root_verified requires old_root == current_root, so the tree is a single append-only GLOBAL accumulator (not a per-session view); inserting from a stale root is rejected (UnknownRoot). Ordered leaves are stored in DURABLE contract state and read via leaves()/leaf_range(start,count)/leaf_count — any client reconstructs the exact tree from on-chain STATE (paginated, so it scales), reload-safe + multi-user-correct, with NO dependency on RPC event retention. Leaf/root entries get their TTL extended (~31d) on each insert so a long-lived pool stays readable. The frontend re-syncs + auto-retries (3x) on the concurrent-deposit race. Verified live across independent sessions: leaves accumulate 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, each building on the real current root.
tested.aspPerUser: the ASP allow-list is a Poseidon Merkle tree of 16 distinct approved sources (aspRoot 2e0753a0...); each deposit proves a RANDOMLY chosen source is allow-listed + not deny-listed, bound to the commitment, WITHOUT revealing which — i.e. genuine per-user compliance, not a single fixed witness.
tested.onChainPoseidon: the pool exposes poseidon_hash(a,b) — a circomlib-compatible Poseidon (t=3) computed ON-CHAIN with BN254 host field ops. Live call poseidon_hash(1,2) returns 0x115cc0f5...4417189a, exactly circomlibjs poseidon([1,2]). Proves Soroban CAN compute the circuit's Poseidon on-chain.
tested.unitTests: 15/15 pass (incl. poseidon_matches_circomlib, accumulator stale-root rejection, ordered-leaf storage, leaf_range pagination)

wallet.default: embedded throwaway testnet demo key (non-admin, holds free testnet XLM + minted USDC) so the corridor is usable with NO install — the pragmatic choice for a public demo
wallet.optionalFreighter: frontend/wallet.js adds an OPTIONAL Freighter connection: when connected, deposits/withdraws are signed by the user's own wallet (setWalletSigner), with a one-click testnet setup (friendbot XLM + USDC trustline (Freighter-signed) + USDC faucet from the demo key). Lazy-loaded and fully fallback-guarded, so the demo-key path always works.
wallet.verification: demo-key default path verified live end-to-end in headless Chrome; the Freighter-connected path is code-reviewed and degrades gracefully when the extension is absent, but exercising the real signing needs a human with Freighter installed (headless Chrome has no extension).

onChainPoseidonFinding.claimRevised: Earlier I said on-chain Poseidon was impossible because env.crypto() has no Poseidon host fn. That was wrong: BN254 Fr add/mul/pow host ops are enough to compose circomlib-exact Poseidon on-chain (see pool.poseidon_hash, verified live).
onChainPoseidonFinding.whyTreeStaysProofBased: Measured cost: ONE Poseidon hash = ~13.6M CPU instructions; a depth-10 Merkle insert = 10 hashes ≈ 135M CPU, which EXCEEDS Soroban's ~100M per-transaction budget (and a deposit already spends two Groth16 verifications). So recomputing the tree on-chain per deposit is infeasible — the correct, affordable design is to verify each insert with a merkleUpdate Groth16 proof (one pairing), which register_root_verified already does.
onChainPoseidonFinding.evidence: pool.poseidon_hash + contracts/pool/src/poseidon.rs + the poseidon_matches_circomlib / poseidon_cost_probe unit tests

trustedSetup.phase1: Hermez perpetual powers-of-tau ceremony (powersOfTau28_hez_final_14.ptau) — a real multi-party ceremony, so phase-1 has no locally-known toxic waste
trustedSetup.phase2: per-circuit Groth16 setup + a Tukar phase-2 contribution; all four proving keys and the on-chain verifiers were regenerated together from this ptau so they stay in sync
